title: Fabrication and Implantation of Miniature Dual-element Strain Gages for Measuring In Vivo Gastrointestinal Contractions in Rodents.
protocol: Handle the strain gage elements carefully with clean Dumont #5 forceps.
Secure strain gage elements to the work surface using a small, clean, self-adhesive piece of paper.
Clean the back of each element film with Isopropyl alcohol and allow drying by evaporation.
Apply a thin film of epoxy-phenolic adhesive to the back of one element under stereomicroscope guidance.
Place the opposing back of the second element in contact and align the foil grids immediately after applying the adhesive.
Place the bonded elements in a 50 - 60 °C oven overnight to fully cure the epoxy.
Trim bonded dual elements to a final size of 3 x 3 mm using a #11 scalpel or single edge razor blade.
Disassemble one 30 cm braided strand of three-conductor wire into three constituent wires.
Pair one of the resulting single wires with the like-colored wire contained within a second 30 cm length of three conductor wire to make a four wire cable.
Remove approximately 1mm of Teflon insulation from both ends of each wire using thermal wire strippers.
Tin the wire ends with activated rosin soldering flux and low temperature solder (melting point 183 ºC) using a soldering pencil.
Wrap a small piece of copper wire (~0.25 mm diameter) once around the standard soldering tip.
Ensure that the copper wire extends beyond the length of the standard soldering tip.
Flux just the solder pads on one side of the bonded dual element with a clean 10-0 brush.
Solder one single lead and one of the paired common leads to the solder pad.
Remove residual flux with a clean brush dipped in resin solvent.
Repeat the process on the opposite side, ensuring that the remaining common wire lead is soldered to the pad opposite the original common lead.
Solder gold socket connectors (E363/0) to the free ends of the wire leads.
Connect the strain gage to a recording amplifier to test the integrity of the dual element assembly.
Measure the resistance with a good quality volt-ohm meter.
Resolder inadequate connections at this point with fresh solder.
Trim off any remaining element film.
Insulate solder joints on element solder pads with a thin layer of two-part silicone-rubber epoxy resin.
Partly cure the resin for 20 - 30 min prior to application.
Cut three pieces of 0.5 mm thick silicone sheet to 15 mm dimensions and clean the silicone with distilled water.
Cut one piece of silicone sheet into a U-shape to accommodate the final dual element assembly without deforming the encapsulating silicone.
Coat the inner surfaces of the notch-free silicone sheets with clear silicone adhesive.
Sandwich the dual element assembly within the notch and align outer sheets, then gently press out any excess silicone and air bubbles from the center outward.
Carefully clamp the encapsulated assembly between two blocks of metal bar stock for 24 hr to ensure uniform thickness and prevent deformations.
Reinforce solder joints on gold socket connectors with 3 mm shrink tubing.
Align electrode pedestal within plastic holder.
Secure wires and pedestal with 0.125 inch diameter shrink tubing.
Secure wires and pedestal with 0.25 inch diameter shrink tubing.
Connect strain gage to high gain bridge amplifier using a cable with mated plug.
Adjust Bridge, Balance, and Gain settings on the amplifier according to manufacturer instructions.
Affix the end of the strain gage where the wires exit horizontally to a rigid clamp.
Calibrate the strain gage by placing a 1 g static load on the opposite end.
Anesthetize the animal deeply with thiobutabarbital (100 – 150 mg/kg; i.p. for rats).
Test for absence of paw pinch reflex to determine depth of anesthesia.
Prepare the rat for aseptic surgery according to approved IACUC guidelines.
Sterilize surgical tools, shave incision sites, apply vet eye ointment, and disinfect all surgical areas.
For long duration terminal experiments, make a 1 - 2 cm midline incision on the ventral side of the neck from the inferior border of the mandible to the sternal notch.
Separate underlying strap muscles using blunt dissection at the midline to expose the trachea.
Isolate the trachea from the underlying esophagus.
Place a loop of 3-0 ethilon suture between the trachea and esophagus to form a ligature.
Make an anterior tracheotomy by incising the membrane between two cartilaginous rings of the trachea distal to the thyroid gland.
Insert a 5mm length beveled piece of polyethylene tubing (P/N PE-270) into the tracheotomy site.
Secure the tubing in place with a ligature.
Replace the strap muscles and suture the overlying skin using 3-0 ethilon.
Prior to surgery, thread the four corners of the strain gage with 4 - 5 cm lengths of 4-0 sterile silk suture using a #14 taper point 3/8 circle needle.
Perform a laparotomy by making an incision along the abdominal midline in the skin.
Incise the rectus abdominus musculature along the connecting linea alba to prevent bleeding.
Make a superficial midline incision in the parietal peritoneum to avoid lacerating underlying viscera.
Exteriorize the stomach with the aid of saline-soaked cotton-tipped applicators.
Keep the stomach in position by placing it on a saline-soaked gauze pad at the caudal end of the abdominal incision.
Align the grid of the encapsulated strain gauge in parallel with the circular smooth muscle fibers.
Attach the corners of the gauge to the ventral serosal surface of the gastric corpus using previously threaded sutures.
Begin the suture pattern along the greater curvature of the stomach near the fundus/corpus boundary.
Proceed with suturing toward the lesser curvature along the fundus/corpus boundary.
Ensure that the serosa underlying the strain gauge is neither slack nor overly stretched.
Return the stomach to its anatomical position using saline-soaked cotton tipped applicators.
Exteriorize the strain gage leads at the caudal end of the midline incision before closing the abdominal incision in an acute model.
Secure free wires to the animal for strain relief during manipulation or terminal wire connector attachment.
Close rectus abdominus muscles and abdominal skin separately with 3-0 nylon suture.
Secure leads subcutaneously along the dorsal side of the rat and exteriorize them above the skull in a chronic model.
Place animals in a stereotaxic frame to support the head and elevate the upper torso to reduce respiration artifact during recording.
Monitor rectal temperature and maintain at 37±1 °C using a feedback-controlled heating pad.
Euthanize animals according to AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia after terminal experiments utilizing thiobutabarbital anesthesia.
Amplify the strain gage signal with any commercially available DC bridge amplifier.
Record the DC output signals from the amplifier on a computer using the chart recorder function of any commercially available data acquisition system.
Make a 1.5 - 2 cm midline skin incision from the occipital bone toward the base of the neck.
Separate connective tissue along the midline between neck muscles.
Detach levator auris longus from the occipital bone once the midline is clearly defined and exposed.
Carefully expose the caudal region of the skull using blunt dissection to detach platysma muscle from dura mater.
Use a new 25 G needle to carefully detach the dura mater along the foramen magnum extending bilaterally to the occipital condyles.
Remove pia and arachnoid meninges overlying the fourth ventricle using #5 Dumont forceps.
Expose the brainstem.
Weigh and dissolve thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH) in sterile saline to reach a final concentration of 50 µM TRH.
Weigh and dissolve sodium nitroprusside (SNP) in sterile saline to reach a final concentration of 150 µM SNP.
Using a 10 µl syringe, administer 2 µl of TRH (final dose equals 100 pmol) to the dorsal surface of the brainstem fourth ventricle.
Using a sterile syringe and 27 G needle, administer 150 µmol/kg of SNP through the tail vein.
